nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$, the number of $n$-color compositions of $k$ that do not use the color $2$ equals the number $e(k) = c_{2,0}(k)$ of even colored compositions of $k$, in which only the parts at even positions are colored. In such an $n$-color composition a part $p \ge 2$ has the $p - 1$ colors other than $2$ and a part $1$ has its single color, so their number is the sum, over all compositions…
nodes.title: Avoiding color 2 counts even colored compositions

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$, the number $e(k) = c_{2,0}(k)$ of even colored compositions of $k$, in which only the parts at even positions are colored, equals the number of permutations of $\{1, \dots, k\}$ that avoid the patterns $321$, $2413$ and $3142$, that is, the number of $321$-avoiding separable permutations of $\{1, \dots, k\}$.
nodes.title: Even colored compositions and 321-avoiding separable permutations

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$, the number $e(k) = c_{2,0}(k)$ of even colored compositions of $k$, in which only the parts at even positions are colored, equals the number of strings of length $k$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ that contain neither $01$ nor $12$ as two consecutive letters, do not begin with $2$ and do not end with $0$.
nodes.title: Even colored compositions and ternary strings

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 0$, the number $e(k + 1) = c_{2,0}(k + 1)$ of even colored compositions of $k + 1$, in which only the parts at even positions are colored, equals the sum, over all binary strings of length $k$, of the product of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the string; a string without a $1$ contributes the empty product $1$.
nodes.title: Even colored compositions and runs in binary strings

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 1$, the number $o(k) = c_{2,1}(k)$ of odd colored compositions of $k$, in which only the parts at odd positions are colored, equals the sum, over all compositions $(p_1, \dots, p_r)$ of $k + 1$, of $\prod_i \binom{p_i}{2}$; that is, the number of compositions of $k + 1$ in which a part $p$ has $\binom{p}{2}$ colors.
nodes.title: Odd colored compositions and binomial-color compositions

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 1$, the number $o(k) = c_{2,1}(k)$ of odd colored compositions of $k$, in which only the parts at odd positions are colored, equals the sum, over the binary strings of length $k$ whose first letter is $1$, of the product of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the string.
nodes.title: Odd colored compositions and runs in binary strings

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 1$, the number $o(k) = c_{2,1}(k)$ of odd colored compositions of $k$, in which only the parts at odd positions are colored, equals the number of strings of length $k - 1$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ that contain neither $01$ nor $12$ as two consecutive letters.
nodes.title: Odd colored compositions and ternary strings

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $k$ and $\ell$ with $m \ge 1$, $m \nmid k$ and $\ell \ge 1$, $c_{m,k+1}(\ell + 1) = c_{m,k+1}(\ell) + c_{m,k}(\ell)$.
nodes.title: A recurrence for positional colored compositions

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $k$, $c_{m,k}(0) = 1$: the only composition of $0$ is the empty one.
nodes.title: Colored compositions of zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $k$ and $\ell$, $c_{m,k}(\ell)$ is the number of $(m, k)$-colored compositions of $\ell$: compositions of $\ell$ in which every part whose position, counted from $1$, is congruent to $k$ modulo $m$ gets one of $p$ colors, where $p$ is the part, and the other parts are uncolored. nodes.title: Positional colored compositions

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
